📋 12 Entry Points

NWCU

NWCU Operations — Intelligence Hub, Case Coordination

National Wildlife Crime Unit — UK's dedicated wildlife crime intelligence hub. Priority species: badgers, bats, raptors, reptiles, marine mammals, CITES-listed species. Case coordination across 43 police forces. Intelligence assessment, analytical products, tactical advice. Liaison with CPS wildlife crime unit. Annual wildlife crime threat assessment. Funding via DEFRA, Home Office, Scottish Government. Operational command structure. Joint investigations with NCA, Border Force.

CITES

CITES Enforcement — Permits, Border Force Detection

Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species — UK CITES Management Authority (DEFRA). Import/export permits for Appendix I, II, III species. Border Force CITES team — ports, airports, postal hubs. TRAFFIC monitoring — wildlife trade network. Seizure data — ivory, reptile skins, live birds, traditional medicines. Penalty regime: up to 7 years under Control of Trade in Endangered Species (COTES) 2024. Scientific Authority (Natural England). Re-export certificates. Personal ownership exemptions.

Raptor

Raptor Persecution — Satellite Tagging, Hen Harrier

Raptor persecution — UK's most serious wildlife crime category. Hen harrier — red-listed, driven to extinction on English grouse moors. Satellite tagging — Natural England, RSPB, BTO. Nest monitoring, GPS tracking, suspicious disappearance analysis. Game estate proximity mapping. Poisoning — carbofuran, alphachloralose, bendiocarb. Trapping — spring traps, pole traps, gin traps. Nest destruction. National Raptor Crime Database. Operation Owl — police raptor initiative. Vicarious liability (Scotland).

Poaching

Poaching — Deer, Fish, Hare Coursing

Wildlife poaching — deer (roe, fallow, red), fish (salmon, trout, eels), hare coursing. Deer poaching: night shooting, dogs, vehicles. Fish poaching: illegal nets, rod licence fraud, salmon egg theft. Hare coursing: organised crime, gambling, dogs (lurchers, greyhounds). Rural crime teams — NFU, CLA, police. Poaching priority areas — Operation Galileo (deer). National Wildlife Crime Intelligence Report. Seasonal patterns — autumn deer, spring salmon. Damage to agriculture and fisheries.

Badger

Badger Crime — Baiting, Sett Disturbance

Badger crime — protected under Protection of Badgers Act 1992. Badger baiting — dogs, digging, organised cruelty. Sett disturbance — development, forestry, agricultural operations. TB culling interaction — licensed culling in England, interaction with badger crime enforcement. Sett survey requirements. Badger persecution intelligence — NWCU priority. Prosecution challenges — evidence, location, identification. Badger vaccination programmes. Artificial sett construction. Licensing for development (Natural England).

Bat

Bat Protection — Roost Disturbance, Development Licensing

Bat protection — all 17 UK species protected under Conservation of Habitats Regulations 2017. Roost disturbance — building demolition, barn conversions, tree felling. Development licensing — European Protected Species (EPS) mitigation licences. Bat surveys — emergence, activity, DNA (droppings). Bat boxes, bat lofts, roost compensation. Licensed bat workers. Bat Crime Hotline — Bat Conservation Trust. Hibernation site protection. Light pollution impact. Wind turbine interaction.

Marine

Marine Wildlife — Seal Disturbance, Cetacean Bycatch

Marine wildlife crime — seals, cetaceans (whales, dolphins, porpoises), sharks. Seal disturbance — harbour seal, grey seal pupping sites. Cetacean bycatch — fishing gear entanglement, gill nets. Shark finning — EU finning ban, UK enforcement. Bass fishing regulations. Marine Protected Areas — enforcement. Dolphin harassment — vessel speed, swim-with operations. Seal shooting — licensed fisheries protection. Strandings investigation — Zoological Society of London. Cetacean stranding duty — Defra/Devolved Administrations.

Online

Online Trade — Social Media Monitoring, E-Commerce

Cyber-enabled wildlife crime — online trade in protected species. Social media monitoring — Facebook Marketplace, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat. E-commerce platforms — eBay, Amazon, Etsy (taxidermy, ivory, reptiles). Dark web trade — rare species, exotic pets, traditional medicines. AI-powered image recognition — species identification from photographs. Keyword monitoring — CITES species, code words, slang. International takedown operations — INTERPOL. UK Digital Investigation Unit (DEFRA).

Prosecution

Prosecution — CPS Wildlife, Sentencing, Evidence

CPS Wildlife Crime Unit — dedicated prosecutors for wildlife offences. Sentencing guidelines — Magistrates' Court, Crown Court. Maximum penalties: 7 years (COTES), 6 months (Wildlife & Countryside Act s.19), unlimited fines. Evidence standards — chain of custody, expert testimony, forensic evidence. Digital evidence — CCTV, GPS, social media. Anonymous witness protection. Proceeds of Crime Act — asset recovery. Private prosecution route. Case management delays. Appeal outcomes.

International

International — Europol, INTERPOL, Bilateral Agreements

International wildlife crime cooperation — Europol Environmental Crime Programme. INTERPOL — Project Thunderball (ivory, rhino horn, pangolin scales). Bilateral agreements — China, Vietnam, Nigeria, India. CITES Standing Committee — UK delegation. Financial Action Task Force — wildlife trafficking as predicate offence. UNODC — transnational organised crime. UK bilateral law enforcement — mutual legal assistance. Extradition for wildlife crime. International fund for animal welfare.

Data

Data Governance — Wildlife Crime Statistics, Intelligence Sharing

Wildlife crime data — annual statistics, seizure data, prosecution outcomes. NWCU Intelligence Report — quarterly. Home Office crime recording — wildlife crime classification. FOI readiness — wildlife crime statistics, investigation data. Intelligence sharing protocols — police, NWCU, Border Force, NCA. Data protection — GDPR, Law Enforcement Directive. Information sharing agreements. National Wildlife Crime Database. Biodiversity data integration (NBN Atlas). International intelligence exchange — TRAFFIC, INTERPOL.

Parliamentary

Parliamentary — EFRA Committee, Wildlife Crime Inquiry

EFRA Select Committee — wildlife crime inquiries, evidence sessions. Wildlife & Countryside Act 1981 — amendment proposals. Ivory Act 2018 — implementation review. Animal Welfare (Sentencing) Act 2021 — increased penalties. Kept Animals Bill — live exports, pet theft, zoo licensing. Hunting Act 2004 — enforcement. Environment Act 2021 — biodiversity duty. PQ evidence — wildlife crime statistics, NWCU funding, prosecution rates. Lords debates — raptor persecution, badger crime. International treaty obligations.

⚡ 8 Transformation Priorities

1. Intelligence Fusion

Multi-source wildlife crime intelligence aggregation — NWCU, police forces, Border Force, NCA, RSPB, Natural England. Real-time intelligence sharing platform. Case correlation engine — link incidents across force boundaries. Priority species threat mapping. Organised crime group identification. Seasonal pattern analysis. Target: intelligence-to-action latency from 14 days to 48 hours, cross-force case correlation accuracy above 90%.

2. Satellite Monitoring

Drone/satellite raptor nest monitoring — hen harrier, peregrine, golden eagle. GPS tag data analysis — suspicious disappearance detection, proximity to game estates. Habitat surveillance — moorland burning, illegal trapping sites. Thermal imaging for night poaching detection. Satellite imagery for sett disturbance. Target: raptor nest monitoring coverage from 15% to 60%, suspicious disappearance detection within 6 hours, illegal activity identification accuracy above 85%.

3. Online Trade Detection

AI social media crawling — Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat wildlife trade detection. Marketplace monitoring — eBay, Amazon, Etsy for prohibited species. Image recognition — species identification from photographs, ivory vs. bone, reptile species. Keyword/code word monitoring — slang, euphemisms, dark web forums. Automated takedown request generation. Target: online wildlife trade detection from manual (200/month) to automated (5,000/month), takedown success rate above 80%.

4. CITES Automation

CITES permit processing automation — application, validation, issuance. Species identification AI — DNA barcoding, morphological analysis, image classification. Risk profiling — high-risk shipments, suspicious traders, historical seizure data. Border Force screening integration — X-ray, sniffer dog coordination. Real-time permit verification at ports. Target: permit processing from 15 days to 3 days, species identification accuracy above 95%, high-risk shipment detection rate above 90%.

5. Forensic Intelligence

Wildlife forensic DNA databases — feather, ivory, bone, fur, ash analysis matching. Stable isotope analysis — geographic origin determination. Microscopic analysis — species, age, processing method. Forensic evidence chain of custody management. Expert witness database. Prosecution evidence bundling. Target: forensic turnaround from 90 days to 21 days, DNA match rate above 85%, prosecution evidence quality score above 90%.

6. Prosecution Support

CPS wildlife crime evidence bundling — automated case file assembly. Sentencing guideline AI — offence severity, aggravating/mitigating factors, precedent analysis. Witness statement quality checking. Expert witness coordination. Digital evidence management — CCTV, GPS, social media preservation. Proceeds of Crime Act asset recovery support. Target: case preparation from 6 months to 8 weeks, conviction rate from 65% to 85%, sentencing consistency above 90%.

7. Predictive Poaching

Poaching hotspot analysis — spatial, temporal, species-based pattern prediction. Seasonal risk mapping — deer (autumn), salmon (spring), hares (winter). Rural crime pattern recognition — vehicle movements, lighting, GPS data. Farm/park estate vulnerability assessment. Police patrol optimisation. Community reporting integration. Target: poaching incident prediction accuracy above 75%, patrol deployment efficiency increase 40%, rural crime reporting increase 30%.

8. Parliamentary Intelligence

Automated EFRA Committee reporting — wildlife crime statistics, prosecution outcomes, NWCU performance. PQ evidence generator — caseload stats, seizure data, international cooperation metrics. Real-time wildlife crime dashboard — force-by-force breakdown, species-by-species analysis. Legislative impact assessment — Ivory Act, Wildlife & Countryside Act amendments. Target: monthly automated parliamentary briefing on wildlife crime performance, EFRA evidence response time from 3 weeks to 5 days.

🚫 Red Lines (Never Crossed)

  • ❌ No wildlife surveillance without legal authority — all surveillance operations must be authorised under RIPA/Investigatory Powers Act 2016; AI monitoring tools cannot bypass lawful authorisation requirements
  • ❌ No CITES specimen seizure without CITES officer authorisation — seizures of CITES-listed species must be authorised by a designated CITES officer; AI risk profiling cannot trigger seizure without human officer decision
  • ❌ No species identification AI without expert zoological validation — AI species identification results must be validated by qualified zoologist or forensic expert before use as prosecution evidence
  • ❌ No intelligence sharing without data protection impact assessment — all intelligence sharing between agencies must complete DPIA under Law Enforcement Directive; automated sharing cannot bypass individual assessment
  • ❌ No prosecution without CPS wildlife crime unit review — all wildlife crime prosecutions must be reviewed by CPS specialist wildlife crime prosecutors; AI cannot recommend prosecution without CPS authorisation
  • ❌ No undercover operation without authorisation under Regulation of Investigatory Powers — all undercover wildlife crime operations must be authorised under RIPA with appropriate authorising officer approval
